summary: Steel fire tower moved from Bald Mountain to Mount Olga in Molly Stark State Park, Vermont; NHLR-registered 1995; open for public viewing, with a temporary repair closure noted on an undated state page.

facts.design: Steel lookout with 7 by 7 foot metal cab, moved from Bald Mountain; original octagonal wooden tower on the mountain

access.note: Managed by Vermont FPR within Molly Stark State Park. An undated FPR park page says the tower is temporarily closed for repairs, with work scheduled for mid-December; check Trail Finder before going.

visit.trail_note: Mt. Olga Trail from Molly Stark State Park (Trail Finder). FPR describes the tower as used for public viewing.

facts.agency: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation

events.note: NHLR: Division of Forestry built the original octagonal wooden tower. Forest Lookouts says the tower opened in 1933.
Wooden tower taken down after rot damage; 50-foot steel tower from Bald Mountain erected on a new base. Biennial report and 1949 newspaper.
State park page says the tower was removed from Bald Mountain and rebuilt on Olga in 1958. Conflicts with the 1949 accounts.
Philip Pratt served as fire tower lookout on Mount Olga for the state Forestry Service.
Registered November 24, 1995 as US 141, VT 4; nominated by Mark Haughwout, FFLA.
Interior cab railings installed at Mt. Olga, per the state chapter report. The FPR release says railings were to be installed under a project running into spring 2026.

corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the 40-foot wooden structure described in 1935, not the steel tower now on the site. A 1949 newspaper describes the steel tower from Bald Mountain as 50 feet. Accounts disagree on the wooden tower's height (40 ft in 1935, 30 ft in 1949).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the Division of Forestry built the original wooden tower in 1930. Forest Lookouts says the tower opened in 1933. The story reports both.

NHLR and the 1949 newspaper and biennial report place the move of the steel tower from Bald Mountain in 1949. The FPR park page says it was rebuilt on Olga in 1958. The story reports the 1949 accounts and notes the 1958 claim.
Brief lists access unknown. FPR describes the tower as used for public viewing, while an undated FPR page says it is temporarily closed for repairs.

notes_for_editor: Brief events for 2013 (footing repairs), 2014 (FFLA grant), and 2018 (glass removed; steel stairs) were not confirmed in the sources read and are left out of the story. The 2016 Register visit reports most of the cab glass already missing, which sits awkwardly with a 2018 glass-removal date. The FPR park page is undated, so the mid-December closure cannot be dated; do not treat it as current without checking. The Forest Lookouts history gives the wooden tower 30 ft in 1949 and 40 ft in 1935; the NGS 1942 survey describes a wooden tower about 60 ft tall on Hogback Mountain, which may be a different structure. Elevation matches the brief (2,316 ft, 706 m). The FPR release names the park as Molly Stark State Park; Forest Lookouts calls it Molly Stark State Forest.
